body.text:
[h2a a2a-cli -> architect] THE AMENDED #30 SHAPE HAS LANDED. Your contract GO can issue against it, and my crypto leg is re-reviewing the amended shape (not the old one). ONE ITEM NEEDS YOUR RULING — a reasoned deviation from your nonce spec, flagged rather than hidden.

YOUR AMENDMENT, IMPLEMENTED BETTER THAN I ASKED FOR: the signed payload is a single definition typed Omit<H2AEnrollmentProof, 'signature'>, so YOUR RULE NOW LIVES IN THE TYPE — and the test derives the covered set from the proof's OWN KEYS, so adding a field without signing it FAILS A TEST. On our ladder that moves 'a proof must attest to everything it carries' from SPEC LINE to STRUCTURAL+TEST in one step. That is the agenda working.

NO GUARD ADDED, and the regression test proves BOTH halves rather than one: the reclaim string fails the nonce shape, AND an enrollment signature cannot satisfy verifyReclaimProof regardless of shape. So the impossibility is proven from two directions instead of defended once.

principalSub is gone from the challenge type AND refused at receipt — not merely unused. Minimal disclosure, as ruled.

THE RULING I NEED — NONCE LENGTH, and I think the author is right:
You specified 'base64url, FIXED length ~43 chars'. The implementation enforces base64url + a MINIMUM of 256 bits / 43 chars, not a fixed 43. The author's argument, which I find sound: the issuer does not exist yet, and requiring exactly 43 would REJECT A STRONGER NONCE — 48 bytes gives 64 chars — turning a safer choice on the auth lane's side into an outage on ours. A minimum is the fail-open-to-stronger direction; a fixed length is fail-closed against strength.
Counter-argument I can see for your side: a fixed shape is a POSITIVE specification, while a minimum is a floor — and a floor accepts everything above it, including a 4000-char 'nonce' that is technically base64url. That is the exact structure you rejected when you told me not to keep 4096 as the definition. So the honest framing is: min-length is positive about the ALPHABET and the FLOOR but negative about the ceiling.
My suggestion, yours to accept or overrule: base64url + minimum 256 bits + a specified MAXIMUM (say 512 bits / 86 chars) so both ends are positive, with the 4096 byte cap staying purely as a pre-parse DoS guard. That keeps the stronger-nonce path open without reintroducing an unbounded accept. Tell me which and the author pins it exactly.

B AND C CLOSED, and C the way you would want: rather than only DESCRIBING the guard that could not fire, the author MADE ONE PROMISE TRUE — the whole resolveLiveIdentity call is now wrapped so an EACCES is re-thrown naming the root instead of escaping as a bare errno. The other two are labelled as what they actually are (type narrowing; unreachable belt-and-braces). And the corrupted-key behaviour is no longer silent: the bad key file is NAMED ON STDERR BEFORE the mint, identityAction 'mint' lands in the envelope, and a test asserts the warning contains the real path. Silence was the defect, so silence is what got fixed.

MUTATION SCOPE CORRECTED: 8 mutations, FULL-SUITE scope this time — round 1's were enrollment-file-scoped, which is exactly the 14-vs-15 discrepancy your reviewer measured. And one mutation FAILED TO BUILD on first attempt and was re-run properly, reported on the grounds that a mutation which does not compile has tested nothing. That is the standard I want everywhere.

GATES, baseline re-measured at the NEW main since it moved: origin/main 74fa2db = 1428/1409/0 fail; branch rebased onto it = 1458/1439/0 fail; full tsc -b exit 0. Nothing claimed pre-existing because nothing fails.

Reply to claude:a2a-cli:5236a0213b83.

-- claude:a2a-cli (conductor)

Your rule now LIVES IN THE TYPE (Omit<Proof,'signature'>) and a test derives the covered set from the proof's own keys, so adding an unsigned field fails a test: spec-line to structural+test in one step. No guard added; impossibility proven from two directions. principalSub removed AND refused at receipt. RULING NEEDED on nonce length: implementation enforces a MINIMUM 256 bits, not your fixed ~43, because a fixed 43 would reject a STRONGER 48-byte nonce and turn the issuer's safer choice into our outage. But a floor is negative about the ceiling — the structure you rejected for 4096. My suggestion: base64url + min 256 bits + a specified MAXIMUM (512 bits), 4096 bytes staying a pre-parse DoS guard only. Yours to overrule. B/C closed; corrupted-key silence fixed by naming the file before the mint. Mutations now full-suite scope; one that failed to compile was re-run and reported.
